preamble: Fortition of the palatal glide /j/ to the voiced alveolar affricate /dz/. The textbook case is Greek: Proto-Indo-European word-initial *y- has a double reflex in Greek, aspirate h- in some words (relative ὅς < *yos) and Proto-Hellenic *dz- in others, written ζ. The affricate stage is reconstructed for Proto-Hellenic; Classical Attic ζ was already metathesized to [zd]. Outside Hellenic, Latin j- normally strengthened to [dʒ] (Italian, Friulian) rather than [dz], so the exact /j/ > /dz/ outcome is rare.

examples.note: Word-initial *y- strengthened to the affricate *dz-; 5th-century BCE Attic pronounced ζ as [zd].
Same development; cf. Persian jow 'barley' from the same root.
Cognate with English yeast; Greek ζ continues the *dz- reflex of *y-.

sources: Beekes, R. (2010). Etymological Dictionary of Greek. Brill. https://doi.org/10.1163/1877-0495_ei10
